title: auriga-industries-private-deploy-scaling-scenarios-wip
content:
PURPOSE

This is a working draft for the Auriga Industries private deployment: sizing scenarios, Terraform module notes, and upgrade/cutover approach. Focus is on a resilient VPC-onprem topology (hybrid with cloud-control-plane), predictable inference latency (95th pct <= 180ms for short-chat path), and a safe terraform upgrade story that doesn’t require full cluster reprovisioning.

STATUS / CONTEXT

- Customer: Auriga Industries (manufacturing analytics)
- Use case: real-time inspection assistant + batch re-ranking jobs. Spiky daytime traffic (8am-6pm) with nightly batch scoring.
- Need: VPC private control-plane, on-prem GPU racks (H100 preferred), KMS/HSM integration, strict audit logging.
- This doc is a WIP: high-level numbers, open questions flagged with TODO.

ASSUMPTIONS

1) Traffic profile
   - Peak concurrent inference requests: 850 small-chat (avg prompt 60 tokens) + 120 long-runner (avg prompt 2k tokens) per minute.
   - Target p95 latency: <= 180ms for small-chat, <= 1.8s for long-runner.
   - Batch jobs (night) throughput: 20M tokens over 6 hours.

2) Model mix
   - Primary: open LLM 13B quantized (4-bit/ptq) for chat path.
   - Secondary: 70B encoder-decoder for long contextual runs (fp16).

3) Hardware chosen (initial sizing)
   - H100x3 nodes as inference nodes for large models; each node: 4x H100 SXM, 1TB NVMe, 1TB system RAM, 512GB GPU RAM aggregate.
   - A100-80GB fallback pool for cheaper long-tail requests (3 nodes).

4) Network & storage
   - Private VPC with 10.0.0.0/16 internal CIDR.
   - NVMe local instance storage for model replicas; shared S3-compatible object store for artifacts/backups.

CAPACITY ESTIMATES (ballpark)

- Small-chat (13B quantized): ~12k tokens/sec per H100 node with batching optimized for 8-12ms per token at target seq length. Expect to host 8 concurrent model shards per node -> approx 96k tokens/sec cluster if we start with 6 H100 nodes.
- Long-runner (70B fp16): each 4xH100 node can handle ~40 concurrent streams at ~10-20 tokens/sec depending on context. Plan for 4 nodes for long-runner pool.
- Suggested initial cluster: 10 inference nodes (6 primary H100 nodes, 4 heavy-context H100 nodes), 3 fallback A100 nodes, 2 control-plane VM servers for operator tools and stateful services.

Terraform module notes (module/auriga-edge)

- module naming: auriga-edge-network, auriga-edge-infra, auriga-edge-inference, auriga-edge-monitoring, auriga-edge-kms-integration. Keep modules small and composable.
- state: remote backend on customer-controlled S3 (minio) + Dynamo-style locking (consul or dynamodb if hybrid cloud available).
- variables to expose (minimal): cluster_size_map (map of role -> count), gpu_type, nvme_size_gb, kms_key_id, audit_log_bucket, vpc_cidr. Avoid exposing internals like instance_types list unless explicitly requested.
- outputs: node_ips, model_store_bucket, kms_key_arn, ci_deploy_token (sensitive).
- Versioning: tag module releases with semver; maintain a migration guide for breaking changes.
- Immutable vs mutable resources: prefer mutable when it can avoid instance recreation (e.g., allow in-place security group updates). For kernel-level changes that force recreation (instance_type change), provide documented plan and drain steps.

Terraform upgrade plan (high-level)

1) Preflight checks (automated): inventory check, infra-state snapshot, disk-space & model cache health, node GPU driver version check.
2) Canary path: upgrade 1 node in each pool (inference + control) to validate kernels/driver combo, then roll 10%/30%/100% with health checks.
3) Model pinning: new runtime may change model execution path—always deploy new runtime with ability to fallback to pinned older model variant.
4) State migrations: run terraform plan with --target on change-lists for staged rollout; avoid single plan with all resources.
5) Rollback: keep last-known-good AMI image and terraform state snapshot to reapply previous count/instance_types quickly.

Operational runbook snippets

- Drain node: mark node as scheduled for drain via control-plane API -> wait for KV cache flush -> migrate active sessions to other nodes (use short-circuit fallback to cloud-hosted small instances for spikes).
- Model eviction policy: LRU by usage with weighted pins for high-SLO models. Provide config flag for 'pin_to_node' for regulatory models.
- Health metrics to collect: gpu_utilization, gpu_mem_used, qps_per_model, p95_latency_per_route, model_cache_hit_rate, nvme_iops, kernel_gpu_errors.

Security & compliance

- KMS/HSM integration: use customer HSM for model encryption keys; Terraform module should accept kms_key_id and create IAM role for control-plane to use key.
- Audit logs: ship all inference request metadata (token counts, model id, request id) to audit S3 with object lifecycle 7 years per Auriga policy. Logs must be encrypted and have checksum verification on rollups.

Architecture Q&A (customer responses & open items)

Q: Do you require air-gap (no internet) or hybrid (private control plane but occasional cloud egress)?
A: Auriga confirmed hybrid allowed but outbound only to Redwood control-plane with strict allow-list. TODO: customer to provide egress proxy FQDNs.

Q: Are GPUs single-tenant or can multiple customers share nodes?
A: Single-tenant preferred for regulatory workloads; multi-tenant allowed for internal non-PII workloads.

Q: Preferred DR/Failover region?
A: Auriga requires cross-site failover to DR colo within same country. Terraform should provision cross-site route policies and replication tasks.

Open items / TODOs

- Finalize exact HSM model and test client drivers (Security team action).
- Run microbenchmarks with Auriga sample prompt corpus to confirm tokens/sec numbers (Perf team).
- Agree retention length for KV cache warmup and model prefetch windows.
- Confirm policy for rolling out quantized vs fp16 models for mixed-precision pipelines.

Cutover checklist (high level)

1) Pre-cutover: freeze model pushes 48hrs, run end-to-end smoke tests, snapshot terraform state, export audit logs.
2) Day-0: Provision initial nodes (as immutable images), seed model store with pinned model artifacts, run canary traffic (5% production load) for 2 hours.
3) Day-1: Scale to baseline capacity, enable autoscaling thresholds, validate p95 latency and throttle rules.
4) Post-cutover (7 days): daily regressions run and quality monitoring, collect token-level cost metrics and tune batching.

Notes on cost optimization (quick wins)

- Use quantized 13B for chat path to reduce GPU memory and increase replica count.
- Enable request-aware batching windows for predictable daytime batch sizes.
- Warm model cache during off-peak windows to reduce cold-starts.

Appendix: terraform snippets & examples (informal)

- Example variable map for cluster_size_map:
  cluster_size_map = {
    "chat_pool" = 6,
    "context_pool" = 4,
    "fallback_pool" = 3
  }

- Example anti-pattern to avoid: changing instance_type via single apply on all nodes -> causes mass interruption. Instead: iterate by role and follow drain/validate steps.

Contact / owners

- Primary: Sofia Chen (owner)
- Performance lead: Liam Patel
- Security lead: Priya Menon

If you have infra-level objections or Auriga pushes additional regulatory constraints, flag them here and we'll convert into follow-up tickets.

---- END WIP ----
